source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο, ἔχοντες τὴν διακονίαν ταύτην καθὼς ἠλεήθημεν, οὐκ ἐγκακοῦμεν, ἀλλὰ ἀπειπάμεθα τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς αἰσχύνης, μὴ περιπατοῦντες ἐν πανουργίᾳ μηδὲ δολοῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τῇ φανερώσει τῆς ἀληθείας συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς πᾶσαν συνείδησιν ἀνθρώπων ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this, having the ministry this, just as we were shown mercy, not we lose heart, \v 2 but we renounced the hidden things of the shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the word of the God, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience of men before the God.

en.L: Because of this, having this ministry, just as we were shown mercy, we do not lose heart, \v 2 but we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the word of God, but by the open display of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience of {{gender:people|men}} before God.
en.B: So, since we hold this ministry because God showed us mercy, we do not give up. \v 2 We have refused the hidden ways that people are ashamed of. We do not act with trickery, and we do not dilute the word of God. Instead, we make the truth plain, and that is how we recommend ourselves to the conscience of every person, before God.
en.R: God was merciful to us and gave us this work to do, so we do not give up. \v 2 We have nothing to do with secret, shameful ways. We do not trick people, and we do not change God's message to suit ourselves. Instead, we tell the truth openly, and we let each person's conscience judge whether we can be trusted. We do all this knowing that God sees us.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, ayant ce ministère, comme nous avons reçu miséricorde, nous ne perdons pas courage, \v 2 mais nous avons renoncé aux choses cachées de la honte, ne marchant pas dans la ruse et ne falsifiant pas la parole de Dieu, mais, par la manifestation de la vérité, nous recommandant nous-mêmes à toute conscience humaine devant Dieu.
fr.B: Ainsi, puisque nous avons ce ministère parce que Dieu nous a fait miséricorde, nous n’abandonnons pas. \v 2 Nous avons rejeté les pratiques cachées dont on a honte. Nous n’agissons pas avec ruse, et nous ne diluons pas la parole de Dieu. Au contraire, nous rendons la vérité évidente, et c’est ainsi que nous nous recommandons à la conscience de chacun, devant Dieu.
fr.R: Dieu a été plein de bonté envers nous et nous a confié ce travail, alors nous n’abandonnons pas. \v 2 Nous ne voulons rien avoir à faire avec les manières d’agir secrètes et honteuses. Nous ne trompons pas les gens, et nous ne changeons pas le message de Dieu pour qu’il nous arrange. Au contraire, nous disons la vérité ouvertement, et nous laissons la conscience de chacun juger si on peut nous faire confiance. Nous faisons tout cela en sachant que Dieu nous voit.

es.L: Por esto, teniendo este ministerio, así como se nos mostró misericordia, no nos desanimamos, \v 2 sino que hemos renunciado a las cosas ocultas de la vergüenza, no andando con astucia ni falseando la palabra de Dios, sino recomendándonos a nosotros mismos, por la manifestación de la verdad, a toda conciencia {{gender:humana|de los hombres}} delante de Dios.
es.B: Así que, ya que tenemos este ministerio porque Dios nos mostró misericordia, no nos damos por vencidos. \v 2 Hemos rechazado los caminos ocultos de los que uno se avergüenza. No actuamos con engaño ni adulteramos la palabra de Dios. Al contrario, damos a conocer la verdad con claridad, y así nos recomendamos a la conciencia de cada persona, delante de Dios.
es.R: Dios fue misericordioso con nosotros y nos dio este trabajo, por eso no nos damos por vencidos. \v 2 No queremos saber nada de caminos secretos y vergonzosos. No engañamos a la gente, y no cambiamos el mensaje de Dios para que nos convenga. Al contrario, decimos la verdad abiertamente, y dejamos que la conciencia de cada persona juzgue si se puede confiar en nosotros. Hacemos todo esto sabiendo que Dios nos ve.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii, tukiwa na huduma hii, kama tulivyorehemiwa, hatufi moyo, \v 2 bali tumeyakataa mambo ya siri ya aibu, hatuenendi kwa hila wala hatulipotoshi neno la Mungu, bali kwa kuidhihirisha kweli tunajitambulisha kwa dhamiri ya kila mtu mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, kwa kuwa tunayo huduma hii kwa sababu Mungu aliturehemu, hatukati tamaa. \v 2 Tumezikataa njia za siri ambazo watu huzionea aibu. Hatutendi kwa hila, wala hatulichanganyi neno la Mungu na mambo mengine. Badala yake, tunaiweka kweli wazi, na hivyo ndivyo tunavyojitambulisha kwa dhamiri ya kila mtu, mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu alituonea huruma akatupa kazi hii, kwa hiyo hatukati tamaa. \v 2 Hatuna lolote la kufanya na njia za siri za aibu. Hatuwadanganyi watu, wala hatubadilishi ujumbe wa Mungu ili utufae sisi. Badala yake, tunasema kweli waziwazi, na tunaiacha dhamiri ya kila mtu iamue kama tunaweza kuaminiwa. Tunafanya hayo yote tukijua kwamba Mungu anatuona.

decisions.choice: because of this: because the ministry is the ministry of the new covenant described in chapter 3
alternatives: a fresh start with no link to what comes before
decisions.reason: Διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") points back to 3:4-18: the ministry Paul and his coworkers carry out is the ministry of the Spirit and of righteousness, with a glory that lasts (3:8-11), and it gives them boldness (3:12). The "we" is Paul with his coworkers, such as Timothy, who is named with him in 1:1 and 1:19.

decisions.choice: ministry: a task of service entrusted by God, given as an act of mercy
decisions.reason: διακονίαν is the word for service, and here it names the service of the new covenant (3:6-9). ἠλεήθημεν ("we were shown mercy") says the ministry came to them as mercy, not as a reward; Paul says the same of his own call in 1 Corinthians 15:9-10 and 1 Timothy 1:12-13.

decisions.choice: lose heart: grow weary and give up
decisions.reason: ἐγκακοῦμεν means to lose courage and give up under strain (Luke 18:1; Galatians 6:9). The same words return in verse 16 and frame the chapter: in spite of what follows, they do not give up.

decisions.choice: the hidden things of shame: secret, underhand ways that people would be ashamed to have seen
decisions.reason: The phrase τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς αἰσχύνης describes methods kept out of sight because they could not bear the light. It is set against "the open display of the truth" at the end of the verse. The past tense ἀπειπάμεθα ("we renounced") states a settled refusal; it does not say Paul once used such methods. In 2:17 Paul contrasts himself with people who peddle the word of God for profit, and he may have such rivals in view.

decisions.choice: falsifying the word of God: watering it down or mixing it with something else
decisions.reason: δολοῦντες was used of adulterating goods, such as diluting wine. Paul does not change God's message to make it more attractive or more profitable (compare 2:17).

decisions.choice: commending ourselves: their only letter of recommendation is the truth openly told
decisions.reason: συνιστάνοντες is the verb of 3:1, where Paul asks whether they need letters of recommendation. Here he says how he does recommend himself: by setting out the truth openly and leaving it to every person's conscience, with God as witness. In 3:1 and 5:12 he refuses to recommend himself in the way his rivals do.

decisions.choice: lose heart (L); give up (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of courage failing; Balanced and Readable say what it leads to. Verse 16 uses the same words and the same renderings.

decisions.choice: act (walking); dilute (falsifying); recommend (commending)
decisions.reason: "Walking" is a Hebrew way of speaking about how one lives; Balanced says "act". "Dilute" keeps the picture of watered-down goods (m5), and "recommend" keeps the link with the letters of recommendation in 3:1 (m6).

decisions.choice: we let each person's conscience judge whether we can be trusted. We do all this knowing that God sees us.
alternatives: commending ourselves to every human conscience before God
decisions.reason: Readable says what recommending themselves to people's consciences means (m6) and what "before God" adds: God is watching and is their witness.

decisions.choice: nous ne perdons pas courage (L); nous n’abandonnons pas (B, R), here and in verse 16
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the picture of courage failing (m3), and Balanced and Readable say what it leads to. Verse 16 has the same words and the same renderings.

decisions.choice: à toute conscience humaine (L), with no gender setting
alternatives: à la conscience de tous les {{gender:humains|hommes}}
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs {{gender:people|men}}. French can render the noun with the adjective "humaine", which keeps the Greek form "every conscience of people" and already includes women and men, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: no nos desanimamos (L); no nos damos por vencidos (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Desmayar" now usually means to faint. Literal keeps the inner sense of losing heart; Balanced and Readable say the result, giving up, as the English does. The same choice comes back in verse 16.

decisions.choice: {{gender:humana|de los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers the traditional "men" as an alternative; Spanish has the same two wordings, "conciencia humana" and "conciencia de los hombres".

decisions.choice: hatufi moyo (L); hatukati tamaa (B, R)
decisions.reason: Recorded for 4:1 and 4:16. Literal says "kufa moyo" (to lose heart), as Ephesians 3:13 does; Balanced and Readable say "kukata tamaa" (to give up hope), the everyday phrase, as the English says "give up".

decisions.choice: dhamiri ya kila mtu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" is a person of either sex, so the Greek "men" is said with "kila mtu" at every level, and Swahili has no span where the English Literal offers "men".

source.text: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔστιν κεκαλυμμένον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἡμῶν, ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις ἐστὶν κεκαλυμμένον, ἐν οἷς ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἐτύφλωσεν τὰ νοήματα τῶν ἀπίστων εἰς τὸ μὴ αὐγάσαι τὸν φωτισμὸν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς δόξης τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If but also is veiled the gospel of us, among the [ones] perishing it is veiled, \v 4 among whom the god of the age this blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that not to see the illumination of the gospel of the glory of the Christ, who is image of the God.

en.L: But if our gospel is indeed veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing, \v 4 among whom the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that they do not see the light of the gospel of the glory of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, who is [the] image of God.
en.B: If our gospel is veiled at all, it is veiled from those who are perishing. \v 4 Among them the god of this age has blinded the minds of those who do not believe, so that they cannot see the light that shines out from the gospel, the gospel of the glory of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who is the image of God.
en.R: Our good news may seem hidden, as if it were covered by a veil. If so, it is hidden only from people who are on the way to destruction. \v 4 Satan, the god who rules the world as it is now, has blinded the minds of those who do not believe. So they cannot see the light that shines from the good news about the glory of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He is the one who shows us exactly what God is like.

fr.L: Et si notre Évangile est aussi voilé, il est voilé chez ceux qui périssent, \v 4 chez qui le dieu de ce siècle a aveuglé les pensées des incroyants, pour qu’ils ne voient pas la lumière de l’Évangile de la gloire du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, qui est [l’]image de Dieu.
fr.B: Si notre Évangile est voilé, il ne l’est que pour ceux qui périssent. \v 4 Chez eux, le dieu de l’époque présente a aveuglé l’intelligence de ceux qui ne croient pas, pour qu’ils ne voient pas la lumière qui rayonne de l’Évangile, l’Évangile de la gloire du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, qui est l’image de Dieu.
fr.R: Notre bonne nouvelle semble peut-être cachée, comme si elle était couverte d’un voile. Si c’est le cas, elle n’est cachée qu’aux gens qui vont à leur perte. \v 4 Satan, le dieu qui domine le monde tel qu’il est maintenant, a aveuglé l’esprit de ceux qui ne croient pas. Alors ils ne peuvent pas voir la lumière qui brille de la bonne nouvelle, celle qui parle de la gloire du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui nous montre exactement à quoi Dieu ressemble.

es.L: Pero si nuestro evangelio está velado, entre los que se pierden está velado, \v 4 entre los cuales el dios de esta era cegó las mentes de los incrédulos, para que no vean la luz del evangelio de la gloria del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, que es [la] imagen de Dios.
es.B: Si nuestro evangelio está velado de algún modo, lo está para los que se pierden. \v 4 Entre ellos, el dios de esta era ha cegado la mente de los que no creen, para que no puedan ver la luz que brilla desde el evangelio, el evangelio de la gloria {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, que es la imagen de Dios.
es.R: Puede parecer que nuestra buena noticia está escondida, como si estuviera cubierta por un velo. Si es así, solo está escondida para las personas que van camino de la destrucción. \v 4 Satanás, el dios que gobierna el mundo tal como es ahora, ha cegado la mente de los que no creen. Por eso no pueden ver la luz que brilla desde la buena noticia acerca de la gloria {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Él es quien nos muestra exactamente cómo es Dios.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa Injili yetu imefunikwa, imefunikwa kati ya wale wanaopotea, \v 4 ambao kati yao mungu wa zama hizi amezipofusha akili za wasioamini, ili wasione nuru ya Injili ya utukufu wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, aliye sura ya Mungu.
sw.B: Ikiwa Injili yetu imefunikwa kwa namna yoyote, imefunikwa kwa wale wanaopotea. \v 4 Kwao, mungu wa zama hizi amezipofusha akili za wale wasioamini, ili wasiweze kuiona nuru inayoangaza kutoka katika Injili, Injili ya utukufu wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, aliye sura ya Mungu.
sw.R: Habari Njema yetu inaweza kuonekana kuwa imefichwa, kana kwamba imefunikwa kwa kifuniko. Ikiwa ni hivyo, imefichwa tu kwa watu walio njiani kuelekea maangamizi. \v 4 Shetani, mungu anayetawala ulimwengu jinsi ulivyo sasa, amezipofusha akili za wale wasioamini. Kwa hiyo hawawezi kuiona nuru inayoangaza kutoka katika Habari Njema kuhusu utukufu wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Yeye ndiye anayetuonyesha jinsi Mungu alivyo hasa.

decisions.choice: veiled: picking up the veil of Moses in 3:13-16
alternatives: a general word for hidden, with no link to chapter 3
decisions.reason: κεκαλυμμένον ("veiled") takes up the picture Paul has just used: Moses veiled his face (Exodus 34:33-35), and a veil still lies over the hearts of those who read Moses without turning to the Lord (3:14-16). Paul grants that his gospel may seem veiled too, but the veil is on those who do not see, not on the message.

decisions.choice: those who are perishing: people on the way to ruin, whose end is destruction
decisions.reason: ἀπολλυμένοις is a present participle: they are in the process of perishing. Paul sets them against "those who are being saved" in 2:15 and 1 Corinthians 1:18. The word describes their path, not a fixed verdict; Paul still preaches to them.

decisions.choice: the god of this age: Satan, the power that rules this present evil age
alternatives: the phrase "of this age" taken with "the unbelievers"
decisions.reason: ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου cannot be God the Father here, since this "god" works against the light of the gospel. Paul names Satan as the deceiver in 2:11 and 11:14, and the New Testament speaks of "the ruler of this world" (John 12:31) and "the ruler of the power of the air" (Ephesians 2:2). Some early Christian writers, wishing to avoid calling Satan a god, joined "of this age" to "the unbelievers" and read "God has blinded the unbelievers of this age"; the word order does not favor that reading. "Age" is the present period of history, which Paul calls "this present evil age" in Galatians 1:4.

decisions.choice: so that they do not see the light
alternatives: so that the light does not shine on them
decisions.reason: αὐγάσαι is a rare verb. It can mean "to see clearly" or "to shine out, dawn". With the first sense the unbelievers are the ones who do not see; with the second the light is what does not dawn on them. The sense "see" fits the blinding just mentioned, but the other sense is also possible, and the meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: the light that comes from the gospel, whose message is the glory of Christ
alternatives: a gospel that is glorious in itself
decisions.reason: The chain of genitives is best read step by step: the light shines from the gospel, and the gospel is the message about Christ's glory. φωτισμὸν ("light, illumination") recurs in verse 6, where the glory is God's, seen in Christ's face. Glory in chapter 3 is the glory that shone on Moses's face (3:7, 3:18).

decisions.choice: the image of God: the one in whom the unseen God is shown
decisions.reason: An εἰκὼν is a likeness that shows what it represents. Paul calls Christ "the image of the invisible God" in Colossians 1:15. The word also recalls Genesis 1:26-27, where humankind is made in God's image; in Christ that image is shown in full, and believers are being changed into it (3:18).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "to them" after "see"
alternatives: "so that the light ... should not shine on them"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a word meaning "to them" after the verb, which supports the sense "shine on them". The SBLGNT follows the older manuscripts, which lack it. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the Greek article.

decisions.choice: god, with a small letter
decisions.reason: The capital letter is kept for the one true God; this is the false god of meaning decision m3.

decisions.choice: Satan, the god who rules the world as it is now
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant (m3), as Paul himself does in 2:11 and 11:14, and explains "this age" for young readers.

decisions.choice: may seem hidden, as if it were covered by a veil; He is the one who shows us exactly what God is like
alternatives: who is the image of God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the veil picture (m1) and what "image" means here (m6).

decisions.choice: le dieu de ce siècle (L); le dieu de l’époque présente (B)
decisions.reason: "Ce siècle" is the traditional French for "this age", the present evil age (m3), and Literal keeps it; Balanced says it in current French. "Ce monde" would blur the word with the one rendered "le monde" elsewhere.

decisions.choice: el dios de esta era
decisions.reason: As in Galatians 1:4, "siglo" is now a century and "mundo" would blur this word with the Greek word for the world; "era" keeps the sense of the present age. "dios" has a small letter, as in the English.

decisions.choice: mungu wa zama hizi (lowercase)
decisions.reason: "Mungu" with a small letter, as the English writes "god", since this is Satan (meaning decision). "Zama" is an age or era, the word settled in Romans 12:2 and Galatians 1:4; "ulimwengu" would blur it with the world.

decisions.choice: imefunikwa
decisions.reason: "Kufunikwa" (to be covered) is the verb of "kifuniko" (veil) in 3:13-16, so Literal and Balanced keep Paul's link back to Moses' veil; Readable says "imefichwa" (hidden) and names the veil.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς κηρύσσομεν ἀλλὰ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν κύριον, ἑαυτοὺς δὲ δούλους ὑμῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Not for ourselves we proclaim but Christ Jesus Lord, ourselves and slaves of you because of Jesus.

en.L: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus [as] Lord, and ourselves [as] your slaves for the sake of Jesus.
en.B: For we do not preach about ourselves. We preach {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus as Lord, and we speak of ourselves only as your servants, for Jesus's sake.
en.R: We do not tell people about ourselves. We tell them that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus is Lord. As for us, we are your servants for Jesus's sake.

fr.L: Car ce n’est pas nous-mêmes que nous proclamons, mais le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus [comme] Seigneur, et nous-mêmes [comme] vos esclaves à cause de Jésus.
fr.B: Car nous ne nous prêchons pas nous-mêmes. Nous prêchons le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus comme Seigneur, et nous ne parlons de nous-mêmes que comme de vos serviteurs, à cause de Jésus.
fr.R: Nous ne parlons pas de nous-mêmes aux gens. Nous leur disons que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus est le Seigneur. Quant à nous, nous sommes vos serviteurs, à cause de Jésus.

es.L: Porque no nos proclamamos a nosotros mismos, sino {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} [como] Señor, y a nosotros mismos [como] {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} esclavos por causa de Jesús.
es.B: Porque no predicamos acerca de nosotros mismos. Predicamos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} como Señor, y de nosotros mismos solo decimos que somos {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} siervos por amor a Jesús.
es.R: No hablamos a la gente de nosotros mismos. Les decimos que {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} es el Señor. En cuanto a nosotros, somos {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} siervos por amor a Jesús.

sw.L: Kwa maana hatujihubiri sisi wenyewe, bali {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu [kuwa] Bwana, na sisi wenyewe [kuwa] watumwa wenu kwa ajili ya Yesu.
sw.B: Kwa maana hatujihubiri sisi wenyewe. Tunamhubiri {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kuwa Bwana, na kuhusu sisi wenyewe tunasema tu kwamba sisi ni watumishi wenu kwa ajili ya Yesu.
sw.R: Hatuwaambii watu habari zetu wenyewe. Tunawaambia kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu ni Bwana. Na sisi, tu watumishi wenu kwa ajili ya Yesu.

decisions.choice: Christ Jesus as Lord: the message is that Jesus is Lord
alternatives: the Lord Christ Jesus, as a name only
decisions.reason: κύριον stands without the article after the name, so it says what Jesus is: Lord. "Jesus is Lord" was the basic confession of the first Christians (Romans 10:9; 1 Corinthians 12:3; Philippians 2:11).

decisions.choice: your slaves: people at your service, because they belong to Jesus
decisions.reason: δούλους is the ordinary word for a slave, as in Philippians 1:1. Their master is Jesus, and for his sake they put themselves wholly at the Corinthians' service. Paul refuses to lord it over their faith (1:24); the rivals he answers in chapter 11 did the opposite (11:20).

decisions.choice: for: the answer to a charge of self-promotion
decisions.reason: γὰρ ("for") explains verses 1-4: their openness is possible because they are not preaching themselves. Paul has been accused of recommending himself (3:1; 5:12), and here he turns the charge around.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Christ Jesus" and "for Jesus's sake"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the order of the names, and some have a form meaning "through Jesus" in place of "for the sake of Jesus". The SBLGNT reads "Christ Jesus" and "for the sake of Jesus". The sense is much the same. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and the English: Literal keeps that a slave was owned (m2), and Balanced and Readable say "serviteurs", since Paul's place in serving them, not slavery itself, is the point.

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Following the English style guide, as in Galatians 1:10: Literal keeps "esclavos", and the meaning decision keeps that they belong to Jesus and are at the Corinthians' service.

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Swahili style guide sets for this word: "mtumwa" (slave) at Literal and "mtumishi" (servant) at Balanced and Readable, since slavery itself is not the point here.

source.text: ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ὁ εἰπών· Ἐκ σκότους φῶς λάμψει, ὃς ἔλαμψεν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Because the God the [one] having said, "Out of darkness light will shine," [is the one] who shone in the hearts of us for illumination of the knowledge of the glory of the God in [the] face of Christ.

en.L: Because God, the one who said, "Out of darkness light will shine," [is the one] who shone in our hearts for the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in [the] face of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: For the God who said, "Out of darkness light will shine," is the one who shone in our hearts, to bring the light of the knowledge of God's glory, the glory seen in the face of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: God is the one who said, "Light will shine out of darkness." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who has shone like a light in our hearts. That light lets people know the glory of God, as they see it in the face of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Car le Dieu qui a dit : « Des ténèbres la lumière brillera », [est celui] qui a brillé dans nos cœurs pour la lumière de la connaissance de la gloire de Dieu sur la face du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Car le Dieu qui a dit : « Des ténèbres brillera la lumière » est celui qui a brillé dans nos cœurs, pour apporter la lumière de la connaissance de la gloire de Dieu, la gloire qu’on voit sur le visage du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: C’est Dieu qui a dit : « Du milieu des ténèbres, la lumière brillera. » Et c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a brillé comme une lumière dans nos cœurs. Cette lumière permet aux gens de connaître la gloire de Dieu, quand ils la voient sur le visage du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

es.L: Porque Dios, el que dijo: «De [las] tinieblas resplandecerá [la] luz», [es el] que resplandeció en nuestros corazones para iluminación del conocimiento de la gloria de Dios en [el] rostro {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.B: Porque el Dios que dijo: «De las tinieblas resplandecerá la luz», es el que resplandeció en nuestros corazones para dar la luz del conocimiento de la gloria de Dios, la gloria que se ve en el rostro {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.R: Dios es el que dijo: «La luz brillará en medio de la oscuridad». Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el que ha brillado como una luz en nuestros corazones. Esa luz permite a las personas conocer la gloria de Dios, tal como la ven en el rostro {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu Mungu aliyesema, "Nuru itang'aa kutoka gizani," ndiye aliyeng'aa mioyoni mwetu kwa ajili ya nuru ya ujuzi wa utukufu wa Mungu katika uso wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana Mungu aliyesema, "Nuru itang'aa kutoka gizani," ndiye aliyeangaza mioyoni mwetu, ili kuleta nuru ya kuujua utukufu wa Mungu, utukufu unaoonekana katika uso wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Mungu ndiye aliyesema, "Nuru itang'aa kutoka gizani." Naye ndiye aliyeangaza kama nuru mioyoni mwetu. Nuru hiyo inawawezesha watu kuujua utukufu wa Mungu, wanapouona katika uso wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: God's word at creation (Genesis 1:3), in words close to Isaiah 9:2
decisions.reason: "Out of darkness light" recalls the first day of creation, when God spoke and light shone in the darkness (Genesis 1:2-3). But the words are not those of Genesis 1:3. The future λάμψει ("will shine") matches the Greek Old Testament of Isaiah 9:2 (9:1 in that version), "the people who walked in darkness ... light will shine on you", a promise of the light God's coming king would bring. Paul seems to join the two: the God who made light at the beginning has made new light in the hearts of his people.

decisions.choice: God is the one who shone: a sentence with no main verb
alternatives: "God who said ... has shone", taking the second clause as the main verb
decisions.reason: The Greek reads "the God who said ..., who shone". The second ὃς ("who") leaves the sentence without a main verb, so "is the one" must be understood. ὅτι ("because") gives the reason for verse 5: they preach Christ and not themselves because God has given them the light.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "light will shine", a saying
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a form of the verb that means "to shine", so that the clause reads "the God who commanded light to shine out of darkness". The SBLGNT reads the future "will shine", supported by the oldest manuscripts, which makes the words a saying of God. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God shone in our hearts: the new creation that happened when they came to know Christ
alternatives: a reference only to Paul's vision on the road to Damascus
decisions.reason: ἔλαμψεν ("shone") is past: God has already given the light. Paul met the risen Christ in a light from heaven (Acts 9:3; 26:13), and the words may recall that day, but "our hearts" is plural and includes all who have turned to the Lord (3:16-18). In 5:17 Paul calls this a new creation.

decisions.choice: for the light of knowing God's glory: the light given in their hearts brings people to know God's glory
alternatives: only the light they pass on to others
decisions.reason: πρὸς φωτισμὸν ("for illumination") echoes the "light of the gospel" in verse 4. The light shines in their hearts, and through their preaching it reaches others; the words do not limit it to either. What the light gives is γνώσεως, knowing God's glory.

decisions.choice: in the face of Christ: unlike Moses's fading glory
decisions.reason: προσώπῳ ("face") recalls chapter 3: Moses's face shone with a glory that faded, and he veiled it (3:7, 3:13). God's glory is now seen in the face of Christ, unveiled and lasting (3:18).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: light will shine
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is future (m1, m3). "Let light shine" would follow a different reading or the wording of Genesis 1:3, not the text Paul wrote.

decisions.choice: That light lets people know the glory of God, as they see it in the face of Christ
alternatives: for the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Christ
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the chain of nouns into a sentence and keeps the open sense of m5 by saying "people".

decisions.choice: aliyeng'aa ... nuru
decisions.reason: Literal repeats the verb "kung'aa" (to shine) from the saying, as the Greek does; Balanced and Readable say "kuangaza" (to give light), which reads more naturally of light shining into hearts. "Nuru" is the word for light as a figure, as settled in John.

source.text: Ἔχομεν δὲ τὸν θησαυρὸν τοῦτον ἐν ὀστρακίνοις σκεύεσιν, ἵνα ἡ ὑπερβολὴ τῆς δυνάμεως ᾖ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μὴ ἐξ ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: We have but the treasure this in clay vessels, so that the surpassingness of the power may be of the God and not from us;

en.L: But we have this treasure in clay pots, so that the surpassing greatness of the power may be God's and not from us.
en.B: But we hold this treasure in pots made of clay, so that the power, great beyond measure, may be God's and may not come from us.
en.R: The treasure we carry is precious, but we are like ordinary clay pots. That way it is plain that the great power at work belongs to God and does not come from us.

fr.L: Mais nous avons ce trésor dans des pots de terre, afin que l’extraordinaire grandeur de la puissance soit de Dieu et non de nous.
fr.B: Mais ce trésor, nous le portons dans des pots de terre cuite, pour que cette puissance, d’une grandeur sans mesure, soit celle de Dieu et ne vienne pas de nous.
fr.R: Le trésor que nous portons est précieux, mais nous sommes comme de simples pots en terre. Ainsi, on voit bien que la grande puissance qui agit appartient à Dieu et ne vient pas de nous.

es.L: Pero tenemos este tesoro en vasijas de barro, para que la extraordinaria grandeza del poder sea de Dios y no de nosotros.
es.B: Pero llevamos este tesoro en vasijas de barro, para que el poder, grande sin medida, sea de Dios y no venga de nosotros.
es.R: El tesoro que llevamos es muy valioso, pero nosotros somos como simples vasijas de barro. Así queda claro que el gran poder que actúa es de Dios y no viene de nosotros.

sw.L: Lakini tuna hazina hii katika vyombo vya udongo, ili ukuu upitao wa nguvu uwe wa Mungu wala si kutoka kwetu.
sw.B: Lakini tunaishika hazina hii katika vyungu vya udongo, ili nguvu hiyo, iliyo kuu kupita kipimo, iwe ya Mungu, wala isitoke kwetu.
sw.R: Hazina tunayobeba ni ya thamani kubwa, lakini sisi ni kama vyungu vya kawaida vya udongo. Kwa njia hiyo inakuwa wazi kwamba nguvu kubwa inayofanya kazi ni ya Mungu, wala haitoki kwetu.

decisions.choice: this treasure: the light of the knowledge of God's glory, carried in their ministry
decisions.reason: θησαυρὸν τοῦτον ("this treasure") points back to verse 6: the light God has given them, which is also the ministry of verse 1 and the gospel they preach.

decisions.choice: clay pots: cheap, fragile, everyday containers
decisions.reason: ὀστρακίνοις σκεύεσιν were ordinary clay jars and dishes, easily broken and thrown away. People sometimes kept valuables hidden in them, and small oil lamps were made of clay too, which suits the light of verse 6. The picture is of the weakness of the messengers, body and all, which verses 8-12 go on to describe.

decisions.choice: so that: God's purpose is that the power is plainly his
alternatives: a result only, with no purpose
decisions.reason: ἵνα states purpose: God placed the treasure in weak containers so that its power would be seen to come from him. ὑπερβολὴ is "excess, a degree beyond measure"; ᾖ τοῦ θεοῦ means "may be God's", belonging to him and coming from him, and the next words say the opposite of the messengers.

decisions.choice: clay pots (L); pots made of clay (B)
decisions.reason: "Earthen vessels" is old-fashioned; "pots" names the ordinary household things Paul means.

decisions.choice: we are like ordinary clay pots; That way it is plain
alternatives: we have this treasure in clay pots, so that
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture stands for (m2) and states the purpose (m3) as its own sentence.

decisions.choice: des pots de terre (L); des pots de terre cuite (B); de simples pots en terre (R)
decisions.reason: French "vase" now suggests a decorative vase for flowers; Paul means cheap, fragile, everyday containers (m2), which "pots" names, as the English does.

decisions.choice: vyombo vya udongo (L); vyungu vya udongo (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Vyombo" keeps the general Greek word (vessels) at Literal. "Vyungu" are the everyday clay pots of an East African kitchen, cheap and easily broken, which is the picture the meaning decision describes.

source.text: ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐ στενοχωρούμενοι, ἀπορούμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐξαπορούμενοι, διωκόμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγκαταλειπόμενοι, καταβαλλόμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἀπολλύμενοι, πάντοτε τὴν νέκρωσιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι περιφέροντες, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι ἡμῶν φανερωθῇ·

records.literal_gloss: In every [way] being pressed but not being hemmed in, being at a loss but not being utterly at a loss, \v 9 being persecuted but not being forsaken, being struck down but not being destroyed, \v 10 always the dying of the Jesus in the body carrying around, so that also the life of the Jesus in the body of us may be revealed;

en.L: In every [way] [we are] pressed but not hemmed in, at a loss but not utterly at a loss, \v 9 pursued but not forsaken, thrown down but not destroyed, \v 10 always carrying around in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be revealed in our body.
en.B: In every way we are under pressure, but not cornered; we are at a loss, but not utterly at a loss; \v 9 we are hunted, but not deserted; we are thrown down, but not destroyed. \v 10 Everywhere we go we carry the dying of Jesus in our bodies, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.
en.R: We have troubles of every kind, but they do not crush us. We often do not know what to do, but we are never left with no way forward. \v 9 People attack us, but God does not leave us alone. We are knocked down, but we are not destroyed. \v 10 In our bodies we always share in the dying of Jesus. This happens so that the life of Jesus can also be seen in our bodies.

fr.L: En tout [nous sommes] pressés, mais non acculés, dans l’embarras, mais non dans un embarras sans issue, \v 9 poursuivis, mais non abandonnés, jetés à terre, mais non détruits, \v 10 portant toujours dans le corps la mise à mort de Jésus, afin que la vie de Jésus aussi soit manifestée dans notre corps.
fr.B: De toutes les manières nous sommes sous pression, mais pas acculés ; nous sommes dans l’embarras, mais jamais sans issue ; \v 9 nous sommes traqués, mais pas abandonnés ; nous sommes jetés à terre, mais pas détruits. \v 10 Partout où nous allons, nous portons dans nos corps la mise à mort de Jésus, afin que la vie de Jésus soit aussi rendue visible dans nos corps.
fr.R: Nous avons toutes sortes de difficultés, mais elles ne nous écrasent pas. Souvent, nous ne savons pas quoi faire, mais nous ne restons jamais sans solution. \v 9 Des gens nous attaquent, mais Dieu ne nous laisse pas seuls. Nous sommes jetés à terre, mais nous ne sommes pas détruits. \v 10 Dans notre corps, nous avons toujours part à la mort de Jésus. Cela arrive pour que la vie de Jésus puisse aussi se voir dans notre corps.

es.L: En todo [estamos] atribulados, pero no acorralados; perplejos, pero no desesperados; \v 9 perseguidos, pero no abandonados; derribados, pero no destruidos; \v 10 llevando siempre por todas partes en el cuerpo la muerte de Jesús, para que también la vida de Jesús se manifieste en nuestro cuerpo.
es.B: En todo estamos bajo presión, pero no acorralados; no sabemos qué hacer, pero no estamos sin salida; \v 9 somos perseguidos, pero no abandonados; somos derribados, pero no destruidos. \v 10 Dondequiera que vamos, llevamos en nuestro cuerpo la muerte de Jesús, para que también la vida de Jesús se haga visible en nuestro cuerpo.
es.R: Tenemos problemas de toda clase, pero no nos aplastan. Muchas veces no sabemos qué hacer, pero nunca nos quedamos sin salida. \v 9 La gente nos ataca, pero Dios no nos deja solos. Nos derriban, pero no nos destruyen. \v 10 En nuestro cuerpo siempre compartimos la muerte de Jesús. Esto pasa para que también la vida de Jesús se vea en nuestro cuerpo.

sw.L: Katika kila [njia] tukisongwa lakini hatubanwi, tukikosa njia lakini hatukosi njia kabisa, \v 9 tukifuatiwa lakini hatuachwi, tukiangushwa chini lakini hatuangamizwi, \v 10 siku zote tukibeba kila mahali katika mwili kufa kwa Yesu, ili uzima wa Yesu nao udhihirishwe katika mwili wetu.
sw.B: Kila upande tunasongwa, lakini hatubanwi mpaka kukosa nafasi; tunakosa njia, lakini hatukosi njia kabisa; \v 9 tunawindwa, lakini hatuachwi peke yetu; tunaangushwa chini, lakini hatuangamizwi. \v 10 Kila mahali tunapokwenda tunabeba katika miili yetu kufa kwa Yesu, ili uzima wa Yesu nao uonekane katika miili yetu.
sw.R: Tuna taabu za kila aina, lakini hazitupondi. Mara nyingi hatujui la kufanya, lakini hatukosi njia kabisa. \v 9 Watu wanatushambulia, lakini Mungu hatuachi peke yetu. Tunaangushwa chini, lakini hatuangamizwi. \v 10 Katika miili yetu siku zote tunashiriki kufa kwa Yesu. Hili hutokea ili uzima wa Yesu nao uweze kuonekana katika miili yetu.

decisions.choice: the participles describe "we" of verse 7: the clay pots
decisions.reason: The participles continue the sentence of verse 7. They show what it means to be clay pots, and each pair shows the power of God keeping them from the worst.

decisions.choice: pressed but not cornered: under pressure, yet never left without room
decisions.reason: θλιβόμενοι means to press or squeeze, and στενοχωρούμενοι to be confined in a narrow space. The picture is of being hard pressed yet still having room to move.

decisions.choice: at a loss but not utterly at a loss: a play on words
alternatives: perplexed but not despairing, without the play on words
decisions.reason: ἀπορούμενοι means to be at a loss, not knowing what to do, and ἐξαπορούμενοι is the same verb made stronger: utterly at a loss. In 1:8 Paul uses that stronger verb of himself in Asia, where he "despaired even of life". Here he says that, taken as a whole, he is never left wholly without a way.

decisions.choice: not forsaken: God does not abandon them
alternatives: not left alone by their friends
decisions.reason: ἐγκαταλειπόμενοι is the word used in the Greek Old Testament for God's promise not to forsake his people (Deuteronomy 31:6; Psalm 37:25, 36:25 in that version). The passive leaves God as the one who does not abandon them; people did desert Paul (2 Timothy 4:16-17).

decisions.choice: struck down but not destroyed
decisions.reason: καταβαλλόμενοι is to be thrown or knocked down, as in a fight or a battle. ἀπολλύμενοι is the verb of 4:3, "perishing": they are knocked down but not finished.

decisions.choice: the dying of Jesus: the process of being put to death that Jesus went through, which they share in their sufferings
alternatives: the death of Jesus as a past event only
decisions.reason: Paul does not use the usual word for death but νέκρωσιν, "a putting to death, dying". Their constant danger and suffering for Jesus repeat in their own bodies the way Jesus was put to death (compare Philippians 3:10; Galatians 6:17). In verse 11 he says it plainly: they are being handed over to death.

decisions.choice: the life of Jesus: the risen Jesus's life, seen now in their being kept alive and finally in resurrection
alternatives: Jesus's earthly life as an example
decisions.reason: The life is that of the risen Jesus. It is made visible (φανερωθῇ) in their bodies now, each time they are rescued and kept going, and it will be shown fully when God raises them (verse 14).

decisions.choice: cornered; utterly at a loss; deserted
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of being hemmed in (m2) and the play on words (m3), and "deserted" for being forsaken.

decisions.choice: bodies (plural); made visible (B); seen (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek singular means each one's body; English uses the plural. "Made visible" says what "revealed" means here: something seen in their bodies.

decisions.choice: People attack us, but God does not leave us alone
decisions.reason: Readable names the people who persecute them and God as the one who does not forsake them (m4).

decisions.choice: la mise à mort de Jésus (L, B)
decisions.reason: The word is not death as an event but the process of being put to death that Jesus went through and that Paul shares in his sufferings (m6); "mise à mort" says that. Readable says "la mort de Jésus" plainly.

decisions.choice: dans l’embarras, mais non dans un embarras sans issue (L); dans l’embarras, mais jamais sans issue (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on one verb and the same verb strengthened (m3). Literal repeats "embarras" to keep the play, as the English repeats "at a loss"; "sans issue" also keeps the picture of being hemmed in (m2).

decisions.choice: perplejos, pero no desesperados
alternatives: en apuros, pero no en apuros extremos
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on one verb and the same verb made stronger (meaning decision). Spanish has no such pair, so Literal uses two words that sound alike in their ending and keep the step from being at a loss to having no way out at all.

decisions.choice: cuerpo, singular
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "bodies" for the plural "we". Spanish naturally keeps the singular "nuestro cuerpo" for something each person has one of, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: tukikosa njia ... hatukosi njia kabisa
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on one verb and the same verb made stronger (meaning decision). Swahili keeps the play by repeating "kukosa njia" (to be at a loss, to find no way) and adding "kabisa" (utterly). "Kukata tamaa" is kept for giving up, 4:1 and 4:16.

source.text: ἀεὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες εἰς θάνατον παραδιδόμεθα διὰ Ἰησοῦν, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ φανερωθῇ ἐν τῇ θνητῇ σαρκὶ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Always for we the [ones] living to death are being handed over because of Jesus, so that also the life of the Jesus may be revealed in the mortal flesh of us.

en.L: For always we who are living are being handed over to death because of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
en.B: For while we live, we are constantly being handed over to death for Jesus's sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our mortal flesh.
en.R: As long as we live, we are always being handed over to death for Jesus's sake. This happens so that the life of Jesus can be seen in our bodies, which will one day die.

fr.L: Car toujours, nous qui vivons, nous sommes livrés à la mort à cause de Jésus, afin que la vie de Jésus aussi soit manifestée dans notre chair mortelle.
fr.B: Car tant que nous vivons, nous sommes sans cesse livrés à la mort à cause de Jésus, pour que la vie de Jésus soit aussi rendue visible dans notre chair mortelle.
fr.R: Tant que nous vivons, nous sommes toujours livrés à la mort à cause de Jésus. Cela arrive pour que la vie de Jésus puisse se voir dans notre corps, qui mourra un jour.

es.L: Porque siempre nosotros, los que vivimos, somos entregados a muerte por causa de Jesús, para que también la vida de Jesús se manifieste en nuestra carne mortal.
es.B: Porque mientras vivimos, constantemente somos entregados a la muerte por causa de Jesús, para que también la vida de Jesús se haga visible en nuestra carne mortal.
es.R: Mientras vivimos, siempre somos entregados a la muerte por causa de Jesús. Esto pasa para que la vida de Jesús se pueda ver en nuestro cuerpo, que algún día va a morir.

sw.L: Kwa maana siku zote sisi tulio hai tunakabidhiwa kwa kifo kwa ajili ya Yesu, ili uzima wa Yesu nao udhihirishwe katika mwili wetu wa kufa.
sw.B: Kwa maana tukiwa bado hai, tunakabidhiwa kwa kifo daima kwa ajili ya Yesu, ili uzima wa Yesu nao uonekane katika miili yetu inayokufa.
sw.R: Maadamu tunaishi, siku zote tunakabidhiwa kwa kifo kwa ajili ya Yesu. Hili hutokea ili uzima wa Yesu uweze kuonekana katika miili yetu, ambayo siku moja itakufa.

decisions.choice: handed over to death: given up to deadly danger, as Jesus was handed over
decisions.reason: παραδιδόμεθα is the verb used of Jesus being handed over to death (Romans 4:25; 1 Corinthians 11:23). It is present tense: again and again their life is put at risk because of Jesus. The list in 11:23-27 shows what Paul means.

decisions.choice: we who live: while still alive
alternatives: "we the living" as a name for believers in general
decisions.reason: ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες makes a paradox: those who are alive are always being handed over to death.

decisions.choice: mortal flesh: the physical body that is subject to death
decisions.reason: σαρκὶ here means the physical body, as the parallel with "body" in verse 10 shows. With θνητῇ ("mortal") it stresses weakness and death, not sin.

decisions.choice: our bodies, which will one day die
decisions.reason: "Flesh" and "mortal" are hard words for young readers; Readable says what they mean (m3).

decisions.choice: tunakabidhiwa kwa kifo
decisions.reason: "Kukabidhi" (to hand over) is the settled verb for this word in the Gospels and Romans 1:24, the word for Jesus being handed over, which is the link the meaning decision points to.

source.text: ὥστε ὁ θάνατος ἐν ἡμῖν ἐνεργεῖται, ἡ δὲ ζωὴ ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: So that the death in us works, the but life in you.

en.L: So death works in us, but life in you.
en.B: So death is doing its work in us, but life is doing its work in you.
en.R: So death is at work in us, and that brings life to you.

fr.L: Ainsi la mort agit en nous, mais la vie en vous.
fr.B: Ainsi, la mort fait son œuvre en nous, mais la vie fait son œuvre en vous.
fr.R: Ainsi, la mort est à l’œuvre en nous, et cela vous apporte la vie.

es.L: De modo que la muerte actúa en nosotros, pero la vida en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Así que la muerte está haciendo su obra en nosotros, pero la vida está haciendo su obra en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Así que la muerte actúa en nosotros, y eso {{plural_you:les|os}} trae vida a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Hivyo kifo kinafanya kazi ndani yetu, lakini uzima ndani yenu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo kifo kinafanya kazi yake ndani yetu, lakini uzima unafanya kazi yake ndani yenu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kifo kinafanya kazi ndani yetu, na hilo linawaletea ninyi uzima.

decisions.choice: the conclusion of verses 7-11: their suffering serves the Corinthians' life
alternatives: bitter irony: we suffer while you live comfortably
decisions.reason: ὥστε ("so") draws the conclusion. The dying they carry brings the life of Jesus to the Corinthians through their ministry, as verse 15 says ("all things are for your sake"). Paul uses biting irony about the Corinthians' comfort in 1 Corinthians 4:8-10, but here nothing in the context suggests it.

decisions.choice: life is at work in you: the verb is understood
decisions.reason: The second clause has no verb; ἐνεργεῖται ("is at work") carries over from the first.

decisions.choice: life is doing its work in you
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats the understood verb (m2).

decisions.choice: and that brings life to you
decisions.reason: Readable says how the two halves are linked (m1).

source.text: Ἔχοντες δὲ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα τῆς πίστεως, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἐπίστευσα, διὸ ἐλάλησα, καὶ ἡμεῖς πιστεύομεν, διὸ καὶ λαλοῦμεν, εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ ἐγείρας τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἡμᾶς σὺν Ἰησοῦ ἐγερεῖ καὶ παραστήσει σὺν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Having but the same Spirit of the faith, according to the [thing] having been written, "I believed, therefore I spoke," also we believe, therefore also we speak, \v 14 knowing that the [one] having raised the Jesus also us with Jesus will raise and will present [us] with you.

en.L: But having the same Spirit of faith, according to what has been written, "I believed, therefore I spoke," we also believe, therefore we also speak, \v 14 knowing that the one who raised Jesus will raise us also with Jesus and will present [us] with you.
en.B: It is written, "I believed; that is why I spoke." We have the same Spirit of faith as the one who wrote those words: we too believe, and that is why we too speak. \v 14 For we know that the one who raised Jesus will also raise us with Jesus, and will bring us, together with you, into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.
en.R: In the Scriptures someone says, "I believed, so I spoke." The same Spirit who gave faith to that writer gives faith to us. We believe too, so we also speak. \v 14 We know that God raised Jesus from death, and we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise us up with Jesus too. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring us, together with you, to stand before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Mais ayant le même Esprit de foi, selon ce qui est écrit : « J’ai cru, c’est pourquoi j’ai parlé », nous aussi nous croyons, c’est pourquoi aussi nous parlons, \v 14 sachant que celui qui a ressuscité Jésus nous ressuscitera aussi avec Jésus et [nous] présentera avec vous.
fr.B: Il est écrit : « J’ai cru, c’est pour cela que j’ai parlé. » Nous avons le même Esprit de foi que celui qui a écrit ces mots : nous aussi, nous croyons, et c’est pour cela que nous aussi, nous parlons. \v 14 Car nous savons que celui qui a ressuscité Jésus nous ressuscitera aussi avec Jésus, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fera paraître, avec vous, en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence.
fr.R: Dans les Écritures, quelqu’un dit : « J’ai cru, alors j’ai parlé. » Le même Esprit qui a donné la foi à cet auteur nous donne la foi, à nous aussi. Nous croyons, nous aussi, alors nous parlons aussi. \v 14 Nous savons que Dieu a ressuscité Jésus d’entre les morts, et nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous ressuscitera aussi avec Jésus. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fera venir, avec vous, pour nous tenir devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: Pero teniendo el mismo Espíritu de fe, conforme a lo que está escrito: «Creí, por tanto hablé», también nosotros creemos, por tanto también hablamos, \v 14 sabiendo que el que resucitó a Jesús también a nosotros nos resucitará con Jesús y [nos] presentará junto con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Está escrito: «Creí; por eso hablé». Tenemos el mismo Espíritu de fe que quien escribió esas palabras: también nosotros creemos, y por eso también hablamos. \v 14 Porque sabemos que el que resucitó a Jesús también nos resucitará a nosotros con Jesús, y nos llevará, junto con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia.
es.R: En las Escrituras alguien dice: «Creí, así que hablé». El mismo Espíritu que le dio fe a aquel escritor nos da fe a nosotros. Nosotros también creemos, así que también hablamos. \v 14 Sabemos que Dios resucitó a Jesús de la muerte, y sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también nos resucitará a nosotros con Jesús. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos llevará, junto con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a estar delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Lakini tukiwa na Roho yule yule wa imani, kama ilivyoandikwa, "Niliamini, kwa hiyo nilinena," sisi pia tunaamini, kwa hiyo pia tunanena, \v 14 tukijua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyemfufua Yesu atatufufua sisi pia pamoja na Yesu, na atatusimamisha [mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}] pamoja nanyi.
sw.B: Imeandikwa, "Niliamini, ndiyo sababu nilinena." Tuna Roho yule yule wa imani kama yule aliyeandika maneno hayo: sisi pia tunaamini, na ndiyo sababu sisi pia tunanena. \v 14 Kwa maana tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyemfufua Yesu atatufufua sisi pia pamoja na Yesu, na atatuleta mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} pamoja nanyi.
sw.R: Katika Maandiko mtu mmoja anasema, "Niliamini, kwa hiyo nilisema." Roho yule yule aliyempa imani mwandishi huyo anatupa sisi imani pia. Sisi pia tunaamini, kwa hiyo tunasema. \v 14 Tunajua kwamba Mungu alimfufua Yesu kutoka kwa wafu, na tunajua kwamba atatufufua sisi pia pamoja na Yesu. Kisha atatuleta sisi, pamoja na ninyi, tusimame mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: Psalm 116:10, quoted from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Ἐπίστευσα διὸ ἐλάλησα matches word for word the opening of Psalm 116:10 in the Greek Old Testament, where it begins a separate psalm (115:1). The Hebrew of the verse is harder and may mean "I kept faith, even when I said ...". The psalm is the thanksgiving of someone who was close to death and was rescued by God (116:3, 116:8), which suits Paul's theme of death and life. Paul quotes the Greek wording his readers knew.

decisions.choice: the same Spirit of faith: the Holy Spirit, who gives faith, the same Spirit at work in the psalmist
alternatives: a spirit of faith: the same attitude of trust the psalmist had
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα can mean the Holy Spirit or a human spirit, an attitude. Paul has spoken of the Spirit throughout 3:3-18, and in 1 Corinthians 12:9 faith is a gift of "the same Spirit". But "spirit of" can also describe a disposition ("a spirit of gentleness", 1 Corinthians 4:21), and then Paul would mean that he shares the psalmist's trust. The two senses are close, since the Spirit produces faith.

decisions.choice: we believe, and so we speak: faith is what makes them speak
decisions.reason: διὸ ("therefore") ties speaking to believing, in the psalm and in Paul's own work. Speaking here is their preaching of the gospel, which goes on in spite of suffering.

decisions.choice: God, who raised Jesus, will raise us with Jesus and bring us into his presence together with you
alternatives: "present" as standing before God's judgment seat only
decisions.reason: The one who raised Jesus is God (Romans 8:11; 1 Corinthians 6:14). παραστήσει means to bring someone forward and present them; Paul uses it of presenting the church to Christ (11:2) and of believers being presented holy before God (Colossians 1:22). They will be raised "with Jesus", sharing his resurrection, and will stand together with the Corinthians.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "raised Jesus"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the Lord Jesus". The SBLGNT follows manuscripts that have the name alone. The meaning does not change. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "with Jesus"
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts read "through Jesus", perhaps because being raised "with Jesus" seemed odd when Jesus had already been raised. The SBLGNT reads "with Jesus", supported by the older manuscripts. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Spirit, with a capital letter
decisions.reason: The capital follows the reading chosen in m2, which is uncertain; the footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: the quotation first
alternatives: having the same Spirit ... according to what is written
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the quotation first so that "the same Spirit" can be explained as the same Spirit the psalm writer had.

decisions.choice: The same Spirit who gave faith to that writer gives faith to us; God
alternatives: having the same Spirit of faith
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m2 and names God as the one who raised Jesus (m4).

decisions.choice: nos llevará ... a su presencia (B); a estar delante de él (R)
decisions.reason: "Presentar" in Spanish usually means to introduce someone; the sense is to bring them to stand before God (meaning decision), which Balanced and Readable say plainly.

decisions.choice: Roho yule yule wa imani (capital R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads this as the Holy Spirit, so Swahili writes "Roho" with a capital and personal agreement ("yule yule"), as for the Spirit elsewhere; "roho ile ile" with class 9 agreement would be heard as an attitude.

source.text: τὰ γὰρ πάντα δι’ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσασα διὰ τῶν πλειόνων τὴν εὐχαριστίαν περισσεύσῃ εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The for all things [are] because of you, so that the grace having increased through the more [people] the thanksgiving may cause to abound to the glory of the God.

en.L: For all things [are] for your sake, so that grace, having spread through more and more [people], may cause thanksgiving to overflow to the glory of God.
en.B: Everything is for your sake, so that grace, as it spreads through more and more people, may make thanks to God overflow and bring glory to God.
en.R: All of this is for your good. God's grace is reaching more and more people. As it does, more and more people will thank God, and God will receive more glory.

fr.L: Car tout [est] à cause de vous, afin que la grâce, s’étant multipliée par un plus grand nombre, fasse abonder l’action de grâce pour la gloire de Dieu.
fr.B: Tout cela est pour vous, afin que la grâce, en se répandant chez des gens toujours plus nombreux, fasse déborder la reconnaissance envers Dieu et serve à la gloire de Dieu.
fr.R: Tout cela est pour votre bien. La grâce de Dieu atteint de plus en plus de gens. Alors de plus en plus de gens vont remercier Dieu, et Dieu recevra plus de gloire.

es.L: Porque todas las cosas [son] por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que la gracia, extendiéndose por medio de más y más [personas], haga abundar la acción de gracias para la gloria de Dios.
es.B: Todo esto es por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que la gracia, al extenderse a más y más personas, haga que abunde la gratitud a Dios y dé gloria a Dios.
es.R: Todo esto es para {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} bien. La gracia de Dios está llegando a más y más personas. Así, cada vez más personas darán gracias a Dios, y Dios recibirá más gloria.

sw.L: Kwa maana mambo yote [ni] kwa ajili yenu, ili neema, ikiisha kuenea kupitia [watu] wengi zaidi, izidishe shukrani kwa utukufu wa Mungu.
sw.B: Kila kitu ni kwa ajili yenu, ili neema, inapoenea kupitia watu wengi zaidi na zaidi, izidishe shukrani kwa Mungu na kumletea Mungu utukufu.
sw.R: Haya yote ni kwa faida yenu. Neema ya Mungu inawafikia watu wengi zaidi na zaidi. Inapofanya hivyo, watu wengi zaidi watamshukuru Mungu, na Mungu atapata utukufu zaidi.

decisions.choice: all things: all that Paul and his coworkers do and suffer
decisions.reason: τὰ γὰρ πάντα sums up verses 7-14: the sufferings, the ministry and the hope they carry. All of it is for the Corinthians' sake (compare 1:6).

decisions.choice: grace, spreading through more people, causes thanksgiving to overflow
alternatives: grace, multiplied through the many, overflows in thanksgiving
grace increases and makes the thanksgiving of more people overflow
decisions.reason: The clause can be divided in more than one way. περισσεύσῃ can mean "overflow" or "cause to overflow", and διὰ τῶν πλειόνων ("through the more") can go with grace spreading or with the thanksgiving. The reading chosen takes τὴν εὐχαριστίαν as the object of the verb: as grace reaches more people, it makes thanks abound. The overall sense is the same in each reading: grace spreads, thanks grows, and God is glorified.

decisions.choice: the more people: more and more people, as the gospel spreads
decisions.reason: πλειόνων is "more", and with the article can mean "the majority", as in 2:6. Here, with "increase", it describes the growing number of people grace reaches.

decisions.choice: to the glory of God: the goal of all of it
decisions.reason: Thanksgiving gives God the honor due to him. Paul's ministry, his suffering and the Corinthians' faith all end in the glory of God (compare 1:20; Philippians 2:11).

decisions.choice: thanks to God (B); people will thank God (R)
decisions.reason: Thanksgiving is thanks offered to God; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: God's grace
decisions.reason: Readable names whose grace it is.

source.text: Διὸ οὐκ ἐγκακοῦμεν, ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ ὁ ἔξω ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος διαφθείρεται, ἀλλ’ ὁ ἔσω ἡμῶν ἀνακαινοῦται ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore not we lose heart, but if indeed the outer of us man is being destroyed, yet the inner of us is being renewed day and day.

en.L: Therefore we do not lose heart; but even if our outer self is decaying, yet our inner [self] is being made new day after day.
en.B: So we do not give up. Our outer self may be decaying, but our inner self is being made new day after day.
en.R: That is why we do not give up. Our bodies are growing weaker and wearing out, but on the inside God is making us new every day.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi nous ne perdons pas courage ; mais même si notre être extérieur se détériore, notre [être] intérieur est renouvelé de jour en jour.
fr.B: Aussi n’abandonnons-nous pas. Notre être extérieur se détériore peut-être, mais notre être intérieur est renouvelé jour après jour.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que nous n’abandonnons pas. Notre corps s’affaiblit et s’use, mais à l’intérieur, Dieu nous rend neufs chaque jour.

es.L: Por tanto, no nos desanimamos; sino que, aunque nuestro hombre exterior se va desgastando, sin embargo, nuestro [hombre] interior se renueva de día en día.
es.B: Por eso no nos damos por vencidos. Aunque nuestro ser exterior se va desgastando, nuestro ser interior se renueva día tras día.
es.R: Por eso no nos damos por vencidos. Nuestro cuerpo se debilita y se desgasta, pero por dentro Dios nos renueva cada día.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo hatufi moyo; bali hata ikiwa mtu wetu wa nje anachakaa, lakini [mtu] wetu wa ndani anafanywa upya siku baada ya siku.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hatukati tamaa. Utu wetu wa nje unaweza kuwa unachakaa, lakini utu wetu wa ndani unafanywa upya siku baada ya siku.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu hatukati tamaa. Miili yetu inazidi kudhoofika na kuchakaa, lakini ndani yetu Mungu anatufanya wapya kila siku.

decisions.choice: therefore: because of the hope of verses 14-15
decisions.reason: Διὸ ("therefore") draws on the hope just stated: God will raise them and the gospel is spreading. So they do not give up, repeating the words of verse 1.

decisions.choice: the outer self and the inner self: the person as seen in the body and this present life, and the person as God renews them within
alternatives: the body and the soul as two separate parts
the old self and the new self
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος means a human being. The outer one is the person as others see them, in a body that ages, suffers and will die (verses 10-11). The inner one is the person as God is renewing them by the Spirit (3:18; compare Romans 7:22; Ephesians 3:16). Paul is not dividing a person into a worthless body and a precious soul; he looks for the body's resurrection (verse 14; 5:1-4). Nor is this the old and new self of Colossians 3:9-10, which are about sin and new life.

decisions.choice: a process going on now: one side wearing out, the other being renewed
decisions.reason: Both verbs are present: διαφθείρεται ("is being destroyed, decaying") and ἀνακαινοῦται ("is being renewed"). The renewal is God's work, as the passive suggests (compare Colossians 3:10).

decisions.choice: day after day
decisions.reason: ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ, "day and day", is a way of saying "every day, day by day". It reflects a Hebrew turn of phrase: the Hebrew of Esther 3:4 also says "day and day" for day after day.

decisions.choice: self
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 3:9-10, "self" says "a human being" without making it a man (m2).

decisions.choice: Our bodies are growing weaker and wearing out; on the inside God is making us new
alternatives: our outer self is decaying; our inner self is being renewed
decisions.reason: Readable explains the outer and inner self (m2) and names God as the one who renews (m3). "Bodies" is narrower than the outer self, which is the whole of this present life.

decisions.choice: give up
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: l’être extérieur, l’être intérieur (L, B)
decisions.reason: As the English "self": the Greek word means a human being, and "être" says that without making it a man (m2); the traditional "homme extérieur" would need a gender setting.

decisions.choice: hombre exterior, [hombre] interior (L); ser exterior, ser interior (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word for a human being, which Spanish has long rendered "hombre" in this phrase and which here means the whole person, men and women alike (meaning decision); Balanced uses "ser", which says the same without the male word.

decisions.choice: mtu wa nje, [mtu] wa ndani (L); utu wa nje, utu wa ndani (B)
decisions.reason: As in Ephesians 3:16 and 4:22-24: Literal keeps "mtu" (a human being, of either sex, so no gender span), the Greek word; Balanced says "utu" (one's self, one's person), as the English says "self".

source.text: τὸ γὰρ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν αἰώνιον βάρος δόξης κατεργάζεται ἡμῖν, μὴ σκοπούντων ἡμῶν τὰ βλεπόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ μὴ βλεπόμενα, τὰ γὰρ βλεπόμενα πρόσκαιρα, τὰ δὲ μὴ βλεπόμενα αἰώνια.

records.literal_gloss: The for momentary lightness of the affliction of us according to excess unto excess eternal weight of glory produces for us, \v 18 not looking us at the things being seen but the things not being seen; the for things being seen [are] temporary, the but things not being seen [are] eternal.

en.L: For the momentary lightness of our affliction is producing for us, from excess to excess, an eternal weight of glory, \v 18 while we look not at the things that are seen but at the things that are not seen; for the things that are seen [are] temporary, but the things that are not seen [are] eternal.
en.B: Our troubles are light and last only a moment, and they are bringing about for us an eternal glory, weighty beyond all measure. \v 18 All the while, we look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen. What can be seen lasts only a while; what cannot be seen is eternal.
en.R: The troubles we have now are small, and they will not last long. But they are bringing us an eternal glory, a glory far greater than all our troubles. \v 18 We do not keep our eyes on what we can see. Instead, we look at what we cannot see. The things we can see last only a short time, but the things we cannot see are eternal.

fr.L: Car la légèreté momentanée de notre détresse produit pour nous, au-delà de toute mesure et toujours plus, un poids éternel de gloire, \v 18 nous qui ne regardons pas aux choses qui se voient, mais à celles qui ne se voient pas ; car les choses qui se voient [sont] passagères, mais celles qui ne se voient pas [sont] éternelles.
fr.B: Nos épreuves sont légères et ne durent qu’un moment, et elles produisent pour nous une gloire éternelle, d’un poids qui dépasse toute mesure. \v 18 Pendant ce temps, nous ne fixons pas les yeux sur ce qui se voit, mais sur ce qui ne se voit pas. Ce qui se voit ne dure qu’un temps ; ce qui ne se voit pas est éternel.
fr.R: Les difficultés que nous avons maintenant sont petites, et elles ne dureront pas longtemps. Mais elles nous apportent une gloire éternelle, une gloire beaucoup plus grande que toutes nos difficultés. \v 18 Nous ne gardons pas les yeux fixés sur ce que nous pouvons voir. Au contraire, nous regardons ce que nous ne pouvons pas voir. Les choses que nous pouvons voir ne durent pas longtemps, mais les choses que nous ne pouvons pas voir sont éternelles.

es.L: Porque la momentánea ligereza de nuestra aflicción produce para nosotros, de exceso en exceso, un eterno peso de gloria, \v 18 no mirando nosotros las cosas que se ven, sino las que no se ven; porque las cosas que se ven [son] temporales, pero las que no se ven [son] eternas.
es.B: Nuestras dificultades son ligeras y duran solo un momento, y están produciendo para nosotros una gloria eterna, de un peso que supera toda medida. \v 18 Mientras tanto, no fijamos la mirada en lo que se ve, sino en lo que no se ve. Lo que se ve dura solo un tiempo; lo que no se ve es eterno.
es.R: Los problemas que tenemos ahora son pequeños y no durarán mucho. Pero nos están trayendo una gloria eterna, una gloria mucho mayor que todos nuestros problemas. \v 18 No mantenemos los ojos en lo que podemos ver. Al contrario, miramos lo que no podemos ver. Las cosas que podemos ver duran poco tiempo, pero las cosas que no podemos ver son eternas.

sw.L: Kwa maana wepesi wa kitambo wa dhiki yetu unatuletea, kwa kuzidi hata kuzidi, uzito wa milele wa utukufu, \v 18 sisi tusipoyatazama mambo yanayoonekana bali mambo yasiyoonekana; kwa maana mambo yanayoonekana [ni] ya muda, lakini mambo yasiyoonekana [ni] ya milele.
sw.B: Dhiki zetu ni nyepesi na zinadumu kitambo tu, nazo zinatuletea utukufu wa milele, wenye uzito usio na kipimo. \v 18 Wakati wote huo hatutazami yale yanayoonekana bali yale yasiyoonekana. Yanayoonekana yanadumu kwa muda tu; yasiyoonekana ni ya milele.
sw.R: Taabu tulizo nazo sasa ni ndogo, wala hazitadumu muda mrefu. Lakini zinatuletea utukufu wa milele, utukufu mkubwa kuliko taabu zetu zote. \v 18 Hatukazi macho yetu kwenye yale tunayoweza kuyaona. Badala yake, tunatazama yale tusiyoweza kuyaona. Mambo tunayoweza kuyaona yanadumu muda mfupi tu, lakini mambo tusiyoweza kuyaona ni ya milele.

decisions.choice: affliction produces glory: suffering is used by God to bring about glory
alternatives: affliction is merely followed by glory
decisions.reason: κατεργάζεται means to work out or bring about. Paul does not only say that glory will come after suffering; the suffering itself, borne for Jesus, is part of what brings it about (compare Romans 8:17-18).

decisions.choice: light and momentary set against weighty and eternal
decisions.reason: The contrast is double: παραυτίκα ("momentary") against αἰώνιον ("eternal"), and ἐλαφρὸν ("light") against βάρος ("weight"). In the Hebrew Scriptures the usual word for glory comes from a root meaning "heavy", and Paul, who knew Hebrew, may be playing on it. The sufferings of 11:23-27 are not light in themselves; they are light when weighed against the glory.

decisions.choice: beyond all measure
decisions.reason: καθ ὑπερβολὴν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν doubles the word for excess: "by excess unto excess". It heightens the greatness of the glory, and may go with the verb ("produces beyond all measure") or with "weight"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: as we look: the outlook that goes with this
alternatives: a condition: only if we look
decisions.reason: μὴ σκοπούντων ἡμῶν is a genitive absolute, which states the circumstances. It can carry a hint of condition or cause, but its plain sense is that this is how they live: with their eyes on what is not seen. σκοπούντων means to fix one's attention on something, not merely to glance.

decisions.choice: temporary: lasting only for a time; eternal: belonging to the age to come and lasting for ever
decisions.reason: πρόσκαιρα means "for a season". The things not yet seen are the glory and the resurrection life of verses 14 and 17, and the eternal house of 5:1.

decisions.choice: light and last only a moment; an eternal glory, weighty beyond all measure (B); small and will not last long; far greater (R)
alternatives: light momentary affliction; eternal weight of glory
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of weight; Readable turns it into a plain comparison (m2).

decisions.choice: what can be seen (B); what we can see (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek participles mean things that are seen; English says "what can be seen".

decisions.choice: wepesi ... uzito
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps the Greek picture of light against heavy: "wepesi" (lightness) and "uzito" (weight), which is also the ordinary word for importance. Readable says "ndogo" (small) and "mkubwa" (great).
